bull_case: Checkout improvements and Venmo/Braintree cross-sell can lift engagement and merchant ROI.
bear_case: Flat active accounts and low-cost alternatives can cap pricing and transaction-margin growth.
thesis: Customer value remains real: payment volume keeps growing and merchants/consumers continue using PayPal at enormous scale. The weakness is that usage growth does not clearly prove increasing wallet share or pricing power.

evidence.claim: Q2 TPV grew 10% to $486.4B and payment transactions grew 8%.
Active accounts were 439M, up only 0.3% y/y.

counterevidence: Branded checkout competition remains intense and active-account growth is essentially flat, limiting evidence of a widening moat.
falsifiers: If transaction-margin dollars contract persistently, branded checkout resumes material share loss, or buybacks stop creating FCF/share growth, the thesis weakens.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Growth is supported by massive transaction volume and merchant/consumer utility, not subsidy or marketing dependence.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Revenue is diversified across branded checkout, processing, Venmo, credit and value-added services; no single customer/product/regulation is fatal.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth despite modest revenue growth

next_checks: Branded checkout growth, Venmo revenue, transaction-margin dollars, active accounts, TPV, repurchases, diluted shares

subscores.rationale: Merchants pay for conversion, authorization, fraud/risk, processing and wallet access; consumer utility remains high.
TPV and transactions are growing but active accounts are essentially flat and branded-checkout share is still a concern.
Scale supports strong FCF, though Braintree mix and transaction expense constrain margin expansion.
